transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’ve realized I’m arranging my life at home around not seeing spiders. I put off doing laundry because it means going into the basement, I avoid the garden shed, and I’ve even paid people to do small jobs I know I could do myself, just because I can’t make myself go into those spaces.
Do you feel anxious or frightened when you actually see a spider?

Yes. If I actually see one, it hits me immediately. My chest tightens, my hands start shaking, and I either just freeze where I am or I back away really fast, almost before I’ve even thought about it.
Have you ever had a panic attack when you saw a spider?

I don’t know if I’d call it a full panic attack, but it feels very sudden and intense. If I spot one, my chest tightens right away, my hands shake, and I either freeze where I am or back out really quickly before I’ve really thought about it.
Are there other situations or places you avoid, besides those where you might see spiders?

Mostly places in the house where I think there might be spiders. The basement is the big one, so I put off laundry. I also avoid the garden shed. And if there’s some small job in a place like that, even if I know I could do it myself, I’ll pay someone else because I just can’t make myself go in there.
Is your avoidance of those places mainly because you're afraid of seeing a spider or because you're afraid of having that intense, shaky reaction you described?

It’s mainly because I’m afraid of seeing a spider. The reaction is part of it, I suppose, because I know I’ll get shaky and freeze up, but what really drives it is arranging things so I don’t have to come across one. That’s why I keep putting off laundry in the basement, avoid the garden shed, or pay someone to do small jobs I know I could do myself if I could just make myself go into those spaces.
Are you afraid of anything else that is similar to spiders, like other insects or small animals?

Not really small animals generally. It’s spiders specifically. I know, logically, that a spider in the corner of an old house probably isn’t going to hurt me, but if I imagine one dropping out of a box or sitting near the washer, it suddenly feels huge and threatening. It’s embarrassing, but that’s the thing that gets to me.
Has your fear of spiders affected your social life or relationships in any way?

Not so much socially, but it has affected things at home. Owning this house is harder and more expensive than it should be because I end up paying people to do little maintenance jobs, or I let chores pile up because I’m avoiding parts of the house or property I need to use. That can be frustrating, and I suppose it does put some strain on things.
Are you afraid of all types of spiders or are there specific types that frighten you more than others?

I wouldn’t say it’s one particular type. It’s more any spider, really, especially if I imagine it suddenly being there near me. Like, I know one sitting in the corner probably isn’t going to hurt me, but if I picture one dropping out of a box or being by the washer, it feels much bigger and more threatening than it probably is. It’s embarrassing, but that’s how it feels.
Have you avoided any activities outside of your home because of your fear of spiders?

Not really outside the home, no. It’s mostly my own house that I work around. I put off doing laundry because it’s in the basement, I avoid the garden shed, and I’ve paid people to do small jobs I know I could do myself, just because I can’t make myself go into those spaces.
Does your fear of spiders occur in other people's homes or only in your own home?

It’s mainly in my own home. I mean, I can feel uneasy somewhere else if I think there might be spiders, but what’s really causing problems is at home. I keep arranging things around not seeing them—putting off laundry in the basement, avoiding the garden shed, paying someone to do small jobs I could probably do myself because I just can’t make myself go into those spaces.
Do you ever worry about seeing spiders when you're in other people's homes?

Yes, sometimes. If I’m in an older house or somewhere with boxes or clutter, I do find myself thinking there could be one there. I know realistically a spider in a corner probably won’t hurt me, but if I picture one dropping out of something or being right near where I’m standing, it suddenly feels much more threatening than it should. It’s embarrassing, but that’s what happens.
Is your fear of spiders something that you only experience in your own home, or can it also occur in other environments?

It can happen in other places too, not just my home. Like, if I’m in an old house and I imagine a spider dropping out of a box, I know it probably wouldn’t actually hurt me, but in that moment it feels much bigger and more threatening than it should. At home it’s worse, especially around places like the washer, but it’s not only there.
Is there anything specific about your own home that makes your fear of spiders worse there compared to other places?

Yes. It’s the basement and the garden shed mostly. Those are the places where I feel like I’m most likely to come across one, so I end up working around them. I put off doing laundry, or I avoid going into the shed, and sometimes I’ll just pay someone to do a small job I could do myself because I can’t make myself go in there.
Can you think of any situation outside of your home where your fear of spiders has caused you significant distress or avoidance?

Outside my home, it can bother me, but the real avoidance is mostly at my own house. That’s what’s been getting to me—I put off laundry because it means going into the basement, I avoid the garden shed, and I’ve even paid people to do little jobs I know I could do myself, just because I can’t make myself go into those spaces.
Is there anything else that triggers a similar fear or anxiety response in you, besides spiders?
Not that I’ve really noticed. It’s mainly spiders. I mean, I can dislike other creepy-crawly things, but they don’t set me off in the same way. Spiders are the thing that really does it.
Is your fear of spiders ever as intense in other people's homes as it is in your own home?

Sometimes, yes, especially if it’s an older house or there are boxes or dark corners. I know logically a spider sitting in a corner probably isn’t going to hurt me, but if I imagine one dropping out of a box or being near the washing machine, it suddenly feels much bigger and more threatening than it really is. It’s embarrassing, honestly.
Can your fear of spiders be triggered by environments similar to your home, such as a friend's basement, even if you're not in your own home?

Yes, it can. If I’m in a place that feels similar, like an older house with boxes or a laundry area, I can get that same reaction. I know a spider sitting in a corner probably isn’t going to do anything to me, but if I picture one dropping out of a box or being near the washer, it suddenly feels huge and threatening. I’m embarrassed by how strongly I react.
Can you think of any other place besides your home where you've had a strong fear reaction to spiders?

Yes, anywhere really, if I actually see one. It could be someone else’s house or a storage room—my chest tightens straight away, my hands start shaking, and I either just freeze where I am or I back out of the room before I’ve even thought about it.
